h2: Visual testing in Chicago: how VT certification works and the inspections that depend on it
html:
Visual testing in Chicago: how VT certification works and the inspections that depend on it

VT certification in the United States is normally employer certification under an SNT-TC-1A written practice, not a licence bought from a school. Atlantis teaches visual testing Level I and Level II as self-paced online theory with a practical examination, and its Chicago training page covers team delivery. For VT inspection in Chicago, Atlantis mobilises crews from Houston and prepares a quote for each scope.

Getting certified. The visual testing course covers the theory hours a written practice normally asks for, and the Practical NDT visual testing simulator gives practice at spotting and recording indications before the practical examination. NDT practice tests help with the general and specific papers. Chicago employers certifying several people at once should start from NDT training in Chicago. Weld-acceptance roles sometimes ask for an AWS Certified Welding Inspector instead; that is a separate personal certification which Atlantis does not teach.

A written practice also sets vision requirements. SNT-TC-1A calls for a near-vision acuity examination at least once a year and a colour contrast check as the employer specifies, and for VT those are not formalities: a technician who cannot resolve fine surface detail cannot be certified to judge it, however good the course results.

Why VT matters in Chicago's inspection rules. State boiler law does not reach into cities above 500,000 inhabitants, so equipment within the city answers to Chicago's own Boiler Inspection Bureau in its Department of Buildings. Outside the city, Illinois rules call for an annual certificate inspection of power boilers, internal where conditions permit, plus an external inspection under operating conditions. Pressure vessels subject to internal corrosion get internal and external examination on a three-year cycle. The commissioned inspector carries out the certificate inspection; VT technicians support it by cleaning, opening and documenting conditions so the inspector's time goes on judgement rather than preparation.

Illinois timing rules that affect how a VT crew is booked for equipment outside the city limits:

  • Owners must prepare equipment for inspection on a date at least seven days after notice.
  • Inspection reports are due within ten days.
  • A certificate stays valid for up to 90 days past expiry while the owner keeps the equipment available for inspection.
  • Heating and hot water supply boilers are inspected every two years.

Plant and mill work. Refinery turnarounds southwest of the city open vessels, columns and exchangers for internal visual examination that decides where UT, MT or PT goes next. On the Indiana shore, Gary Works is preparing to reline Blast Furnace No. 14 from 2026, and furnace relines put shells, staves, tuyere areas and structural steel through extensive visual examination under difficult access. Remote visual tools are used where entry is restricted, and photographs are tied to a location reference so findings can be found again.

Examinations follow ASME Section V Article 9 or AWS D1.1 for structural welds, with acceptance from the governing code. See the national visual testing service, the Illinois-wide picture at NDT inspection services in Illinois, or the ASNT NDT Level III route if you are heading for VT Level III. To ask about VT certification for a Chicago crew, contact the training desk.
